cheng: Heads-up — stress run of mosaic-14b-int8 on nightly loadbench showed a big cost/token jump when kv-cache=true. job failed at high concurrency (4k).
priyanka: link to the failing job and dashboard? what metric spiked exactly?
alex: dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/bench/mosaic-14b-int8/sweep-2026-03-20
summary: p95 latency 2.1s -> 6.8s, tokens/s down ~60%, estimated cost per 1M tokens up ~3x during the window.
cheng: here's the trimmed runner log around the failure:
```
[runner] conf: batch_size=64 concurrency=4096 kv_cache=true
[2026-03-20T02:14:05Z] backpressure: queue_len=5182 inflight=3200 drop=0
[2026-03-20T02:14:05Z] p95_latency=6800ms tokens/s=120000
[2026-03-20T02:14:06Z] stall: kv-evict=true evict_count=2300
```
maria: did we ship any kernel/selection or batching changes in the last deploy that could affect kv-cache hotpath? any PRs rolled?
deploy-bot: rolled: #3421 (kernel-selection heuristics), #3423 (batch-windowing tweak), rollout env: canary -> prod (03/19).
sam: sounds like kv cache eviction thrashing at high parallelism. quick repro: run the same sweep with kv_cache=false and compare. ideally add a warmup stage to populate KV. i can spin up a targeted run.
priyanka: please also add a cost_per_token metric to the eval harness and emit to the bench metrics so dashboards can alert on regressions. suggested query: `sum(cost_usd)/sum(tokens) as cost_per_token` over 5m windows.
alex: I'll open an issue and a small PR to the harness to (1) emit cost_per_token, (2) publish kv-evict and queue_len to the bench namespace, (3) add a canary job with smaller concurrency steps.
cheng: thanks. action items: sam -> run kv_cache=false sweep and warmup-run; alex -> PR to add metrics + canary job; maria -> verify if #3421/#3423 could cause this; priyanka -> add alerting threshold for cost_per_token and p95 surge.
priyanka: ack :thumbsup:
sam: starting a repro now, will post logs shortly.
cheng: good — let's avoid rolling more runner heuristics to prod until we confirm. assigning owners and will coordinate in a follow-up thread. :eyes:
